# Introduction

This file is used to conduct ordinal regression analysis on the survey responses of Recreational fishers from the SELTMP in 2025. Regressions test trends between responses to different ranked 1-10 questions, such as support for MPAs, against whether the respondent would be likely to report suspicious activity

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(ordinal)   # clm() for models and nominal_test()
library(MASS)      # polr() for Brant test
library(brant)     # Brant test for proportional odds
library(car)       # Model comparisons and diagnostics
library(emmeans)   # Marginal means if needed
```

# 1. Prepare data

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Oct-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

#glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter Data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |>
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == "1")
```

# 2. Choose outcome and predictor questions

```{r}
# Specify a single pair of questions  (add in code to filter 9s as NA values for q14)
outcome_var <- "inter_zoning"
predictor_var <- "GBRbp_report"
```

```{r}
# Option A: treat predictor as numeric

# Keep only necessary columns
data <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    outcome = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[outcome_var]])),
    predictor = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[predictor_var]]))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(outcome), !is.na(predictor)) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),  # Note: outcome is best treated as factor
    predictor = as.numeric(predictor)
  )

# Check response distribution
table(data$outcome)
table(data$predictor)
```

```{r}
# Option B: treat predictor as factor
data <- fisher_data %>%
  transmute(
    outcome = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[outcome_var]])),
    predictor = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[predictor_var]]))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(outcome), !is.na(predictor)) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
    predictor = factor(predictor, ordered = FALSE)   
  )

table(data$outcome)
table(data$predictor)
```

# 3. Fit ordered logit model

```{r}
# Ordered logit (set predictor to factor or numerical with chunks in section 2)
m_ord <- clm(outcome ~ predictor, data = data, link = "logit")
summary(m_ord)
```

# 4. Check proportional odds / parallel slopes assumption

```{r}
# Option A: nominal_test() from ordinal package
nominal_test(m_ord)

# If p < 0.05, the proportional odds assumption is likely violated
```

```{r}
# Option B: Brant test using MASS::polr
m_p <- MASS::polr(outcome ~ predictor, data = data, Hess = TRUE)
brant(m_p)
```

# 5. LR test for overall model significance

```{r}
# Null model
m_null <- clm(outcome ~ 1, data = data, link = "logit")

# Log-likelihoods
ll_null <- as.numeric(logLik(m_null))
ll_model <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))

# LR statistic
lr_stat <- 2 * (ll_model - ll_null)

# DF difference
df_diff <- attr(logLik(m_ord), "df") - attr(logLik(m_null), "df")

# p-value
p_value <- pchisq(lr_stat, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)

# Report
data.frame(
  Model = "Ordered logit model vs intercept-only",
  LR = lr_stat,
  df = df_diff,
  p_value = p_value
)
```

# 6. AIC and BIC

```{r}
AIC(m_ord)
BIC(m_ord)

AIC(m_null)
BIC(m_null)
```

# 7. If the proportional odds assumption is violated: generalized ordered logit

```{r}
# IMPORTANT: for a generalized ordered logit, the predictor is usually best treated as a factor with a manageable number of levels.

#SAME PROBELM WHERE FACTORS CREATE CONFUSING RESULTS

# Create a version with predictor as factor if needed
data_gen <- data %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = as.numeric(as.character(outcome)),
    predictor = as.numeric(as.character(predictor))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(outcome), !is.na(predictor)) %>%
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(outcome, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
    predictor = factor(predictor, ordered = FALSE)
  )

# Check counts by predictor category
table(data_gen$predictor)
```

```{r}
# If some predictor categories are sparse, collapse them
data_gen <- data %>%
  mutate(
    predictor = case_when(
      predictor %in% c("1", "2") ~ "Low",
      predictor %in% c("3", "4", "5") ~ "Medium",
      predictor %in% c("6", "7", "8") ~ "High",
      predictor %in% c("9", "10") ~ "Very High",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Very High"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(predictor))

table(data_gen$predictor)
```

```{r}
# Fit the model
m_gen <- clm(outcome ~ predictor, data = data_gen, link = "logit", nominal = ~ predictor)
summary(m_gen)
```

# 9. Compare ordered logit to generalized ordered logit

```{r}
ll_ord <- as.numeric(logLik(m_ord))
ll_gen <- as.numeric(logLik(m_gen))

lr_gen <- 2 * (ll_gen - ll_ord)
df_gen <- attr(logLik(m_gen), "df") - attr(logLik(m_ord), "df")
p_gen <- pchisq(lr_gen, df = df_gen, lower.tail = FALSE)

data.frame(
  Model = "Generalized ordered logit vs ordered logit",
  LR = lr_gen,
  df = df_gen,
  p_value = p_gen
)
```

# 10. Assumption checks for generalized model

```{r}
# Check whether non-parallel slopes are needed
nominal_test(m_gen)

# Compare AIC/BIC for the generalized model
AIC(m_gen)
BIC(m_gen)
AIC(m_ord)
BIC(m_ord)
```

# 11. Run loop across multiple survey question pairs

```{r}
# List of survey variables to test as predictors
predictor_list <- c(
  "GBRbp_advocacyfish",
  "GBRbp_rubbish",
  "GBRbp_app",
  "GBRbp_report",
  "reef_health",
  "trust_managers"
)

# Create a results table
results <- tibble()

for (pred in predictor_list) {
  temp <- data %>%
    transmute(
      outcome = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[outcome_var]])),
      predictor = as.numeric(as.character(.data[[pred]]))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(outcome), !is.na(predictor)) %>%
    mutate(
      outcome = factor(outcome, ordered = TRUE, levels = 1:10),
      predictor = as.numeric(predictor)
    )
  
  # Fit model
  m <- clm(outcome ~ predictor, data = temp, link = "logit")
  
  # Null model
  m0 <- clm(outcome ~ 1, data = temp, link = "logit")
  
  # LR test
  ll0 <- as.numeric(logLik(m0))
  llm <- as.numeric(logLik(m))
  lr <- 2 * (llm - ll0)
  df <- attr(logLik(m), "df") - attr(logLik(m0), "df")
  p <- pchisq(lr, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  # Parallel slopes check
  p_parallel <- tryCatch(
    nominal_test(m)$p.value[1],
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
  
  # Save results
  results <- bind_rows(
    results,
    tibble(
      outcome = outcome_var,
      predictor = pred,
      LR = lr,
      df = df,
      p_value = p,
      parallel_slopes_p = p_parallel,
      AIC = AIC(m),
      BIC = BIC(m)
    )
  )
}

results
```

# 12. Interpretation

For each question pair:

- If the ordered logit model is significant, then the predictor question has a statistically significant association with the outcome question.

- If the proportional odds test is significant, then the standard ordered logit may be inappropriate and a generalized ordered logit should be considered.

- AIC/BIC help compare model fit and complexity.

- Predicted category distribution helps assess whether the model is doing a reasonable job at predicting likely response levels.
